title: Diffraction limit of a circular aperture
references: Rayleigh, Lord, Investigations in optics, with special reference to the spectroscope, Philosophical Magazine 8(49), 261-274 (1879), doi:10.1080/14786447908639684
Sparrow, C. M., On Spectroscopic Resolving Power, Astrophysical Journal 44, 76-86 (1916), doi:10.1086/142271
Born, M. and Wolf, E., Principles of Optics, 7th ed., Cambridge University Press (1999)
validity_domain: Smallest angular separation a diffraction-limited telescope or camera with a single circular aperture of diameter D resolves at wavelength lambda: 1.22 lambda / D by the Rayleigh criterion, 0.947 lambda / D by the stricter Sparrow criterion.
limitations: Assumption resolution_criterion: unstated, the engine takes both; a claim below the Sparrow limit is inconsistent under both criteria, a claim between the two is possible only with the Sparrow criterion.
Single filled circular aperture: interferometric arrays (baseline instead of diameter), speckle and lucky imaging, and super-resolution post-processing are outside its assumptions
Diffraction only: atmospheric seeing and optical aberrations make real resolution worse, never better
